title: Overlapping AI validation of Bitcoin Core governance coding
subtitle: Round 12  |  Research methods assessment  |  November 7 2026

blocks.text: The overlap test supports the main distinctions used in the bounded Bitcoin Core reconstruction, while exposing continuing instability in institutional classification. All three fresh AI contexts agreed on candidate screening for all 24 sampled records. Among 58 one-to-one statement matches, all three agreed on all seven compared labels in 29 cases. Source reconciliation remains necessary because shared labels do not establish correctness and majority voting can miss supported interpretations.

The practical implication is to retain the existing reconstruction, add the overlap evidence, clarify several coding conventions, and qualify the absolute translation-freeze claim. This round does not justify a claim that the entire institutional model or source corpus has been validated.
Design and scope

Three fresh AI contexts independently received the same 24 focal records from six linked 2025 contribution episodes: PRs 32359, 32381, 32406, 32714, 33224, and 33453. The study reused the complete Round 4 sample, comprising 12 purposive records, six deterministically sampled candidate records, and six deterministically sampled excluded records. These are known research materials, not a previously unseen holdout. The identical packet contained 98 entries, including surrounding exchanges, dated guidance, patches, and metadata.

The study froze project specification 0.3, its schema and checker, the source bytes, selection, instructions, and comparison plan before dispatch. Each coder used a fresh context without the parent conversation, earlier annotations, other coders’ answers, or the earlier conclusions. The same inherited model configuration served all three runs; this was not a comparison of distinct model families. Provider snapshot, sampling parameters, token use, and costs were unavailable. The filesystem was shared and access restrictions were instructional rather than technically enforced; coder access records are self-reports.

Each coder preserved a first complete annotation, ran the supplied checker, conducted one source-based self-review, and froze the final output. The first checks reported six mechanical issues for A and three for C; B passed its first check. All final annotations passed the coordinator’s repeated checker, covering 1,952 exact anchor references in total. These checks establish structural and quotation integrity, not semantic correctness. First and final versions, recorded changes, flags, and instructions remain in the evidence package.

A separate fresh context aligned the focal statements with the seven comparison labels withheld. Component text remained visible to distinguish analytical layers, so masking was incomplete. Another fresh context reviewed all 24 focal sources, including agreements, against the codebook and relevant context; it did not receive the prior baseline or agreement scores. After the coding outputs froze, the coordinator reviewed the alignment and sources, reconciled findings, and assessed implications for the inherited analysis.
Agreement before reconciliation

All coders classified the same 22 focal records as containing candidates and the same two as context only. Their focal statement counts were 62, 71, and 70. Forty-one statements had identical spans across all three coders. Source-based alignment identified 58 one-to-one groups, one split/combined group, 13 groups with missing counterparts, and two unresolved groups. Every one of the 203 focal statement records appears exactly once in this mapping.

blocks.caption: Unanimous agreement across the three submitted final annotations
blocks.note: Denominator: 58 one-to-one statement groups. These descriptive rates precede reconciliation and are not accuracy estimates. They do not include component-role, relation, or outcome-claim agreement.

blocks.text: Institutional type showed the least agreement. Overall governance-level agreement was higher, but the difficult majority and transparency statements produced substantial differences. The high overall rate largely reflects routine operational statements and should not obscure uncertainty in rarer higher-level interpretations.

The matched denominator covers 174 of the 203 statement records. The remaining 29 records belong to the split/combined group, missing-counterpart groups, or unresolved groups; they are retained rather than counted as agreements. The two unresolved groups concern how a quoted premise and a tentative 150-byte refinement attach to the focal units, even though the full annotations retain these details in context or evidence. Pairwise results and every group mapping are available in the package. Multiple statements from one source are not independent observations.
Findings from source review
Recognition must attach to a specific proposition

The strongest standing disagreement concerns the conditional advice against removal warnings when no current removal plan exists. The retained 33453 proposal body attributes, quotes, and applies that expectation. This supports the inherited local-recognition judgment even though two fresh coders selected text_only. Local support does not require a binding project-wide rule. Exact assent to a definition of deprecation remains more interpretive: it can recognize an institutional status or simply endorse terminology. The explicit nonblocking-nits reply provides a clearer shared example of local recognition. Sources: 32714-body, 33453-body, 32406-180, and 32406-151.
Documentary support depends on scope and date

General guidance on moderation documents a procedure for warnings and bans; it does not independently verify the particular future sanction announced to a named contributor. Similarly, a later contribution guide supports discretionary merit weighting without proving the exact wording or force of an earlier categorical reminder. Broad maintainer release responsibility and deference on one backport decision are related but distinct evidence claims. Several standing differences arise because coders classify these different levels of specificity under one label. Sources: 32359-115, 32406-169, 32406-252, 33453-018, D_CONTRIB, and D_MOD.
Matching labels can conceal provenance errors

Within the body of PR 32381, a separate recommendation advocates proceeding with PR 32359. Two coders attach closure metadata for the containing PR to that recommendation. Both PRs closed unmerged, so the status labels match while the evidence targets differ. The correction is to attach the referenced proposal’s metadata or retain the containing proposal’s closure only as episode context. The audit also identified pronouns anchored to the wrong predicate occurrence and incomplete evidence arrays. Exact text matching alone did not detect those semantic targeting problems. Findings SA09, SA14, SA16, SA20, and SA21 preserve the repairs.
Higher level claims require bounded alternatives

The statement that a majority decides the winner supplies no electorate, threshold, jurisdiction, or decision procedure. Unknown is the least assumptive target level; constitutional and epistemic readings remain alternatives. The transparency statement more clearly expresses a contested legitimacy expectation, but its target can concern either the foundations of legitimate decisions or recurring decision procedures. The observed exchange does not establish adoption of a new arrangement. A thematic contrast between majority and merit claims also does not prove that they contest the same decision object. Sources: 32359-227, 32359-115, 32406-228, and 32406-229.
The absolute freeze claim faces a counterproposal

All three coders identify a categorical prohibition on translation-source updates after the final freeze and flag a dispute in its application. The proposed workaround would permit a source change while limiting translation disruption. It recognizes the reason for a freeze without independently establishing the absolute rule, a formal exception, or actual final translation processing. The inherited U32 annotation should therefore retain its limited evidentiary status while explicitly acknowledging this application challenge. Sources: 33224-010, 33224-015, 33224-019, and D_TRANSLATION.
Extraction differences need meaning and scope checks

Some inventory differences preserve meaning through different layers or subdivisions, including a user’s mempool-control claim and the distinction between possible future deprecation and a preferred removal schedule. The two unresolved alignment groups concern where a quoted premise and a tentative 150-byte refinement are stored. The full annotations retain those details in context or evidence, but the focal units do not attach them consistently. These are not established wholesale omissions. A shared convention deviation also survives: all three label a repeated literal bot question with a nonquestion speech act. Findings SA05, SA11, SA12, SA18, SA22, and SA23 retain these distinctions.
The central evidentiary boundaries survive

All three distinguish the reported addition of a source comment from verification of its exact wording, an announced moderation consequence from an observed ban, and repository integration from Bitcoin network adoption. They reproduce the supplied sequence of deprecation and warning edits while avoiding a permanent maintenance commitment or a fixed removal timetable. These agreements support the bounded reconstruction. The retained proposal bodies also show explicit attribution across proposals, but absent version histories the analysis cannot date the insertion of every quoted sentence or establish its causal effect on merger.
Implications for the existing analysis

Twelve of the 46 inherited statement units used in Round 11 occur in the focal records. The shared context also permits comparison of the supplied repository-state sequence, but the present study does not independently retest all platform-event findings, podcast coding, the original Paper 1 sample, or the full comparative model. Within this scope, the source review does not require rebuilding the central reconstruction.

The most concrete inherited annotation change concerns U32: explicitly record the challenge to the absolute translation-freeze claim’s application. Two other inherited units, U02 on review weighting and N16 on transparent decision-making, merit a clearer preferred grammatical representation. All three fresh coders used regulative parses; the earlier constitutive representations can preserve related meaning, so this is a matter for explicit harmonization rather than an automatic finding that the institutional conclusions were wrong.

Retain the evidence distinctions already present in the earlier analysis: local recognition of the conditional warning principle, a general documented moderation procedure versus a particular announced sanction, and documented release responsibilities versus deference on one backport decision. The separate baseline-impact ledger identifies proposed changes and retained findings. It does not alter the inherited files or manuscript.
What the working paper can claim

The study now has an overlapping AI repeatability test on a defined sample, with preserved independent submissions, mechanical checks, explicit proposition alignment, and revisable source-based reconciliation. The results support presenting these stages as an integrated analytical method. They also identify where the method needs sharper conventions: recognition versus ordinary assent, the scope and date of documentary support, institutional type, analytical layers, and higher-level governance claims.

The evidence does not establish cross-model robustness, population accuracy, a human reference standard, causal identification, or superior speed and cost. No numerical threshold defined a pass. The comparison measures consistency conditional on this sample, packet, specification, and workflow. Source reconciliation is another inspectable AI judgment, and defensible alternatives remain visible.
Evidence package

The evidence package contains the frozen protocol and sources, first and final annotations, comparisons, independent audit, reconciled findings, and baseline-impact ledger. Its README identifies the principal files and reproduction commands. Scripts verify integrity and recompute agreement; the source interpretations remain inspectable judgments.
